A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyVec research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support comparison across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and generation results, component ablations, transferability experiments, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds linear-probing comparisons, additional model configurations, permutation controls, and construction/optimization timing.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same EQR extraction, projected-representation segmentation, REINFORCE position selection, and weighted vector injection. No proposed algorithm component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six classification datasets and six generation tasks. The added models, permutation controls, and timing experiment use retained task coverage; they do not introduce new datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add Linear Probing across all three original models and 4/8/16-shot settings. Table 4 removes MTV, whose v1 average was 58.32 versus DyVec's 60.48, while retaining FV and TV. This materially changes both comparison groups. v2's residual mention of MTV in Section 6.1 does not correspond to reported MTV results.

E3.justification: Tables 4–5 add GPT-J-6B and LLaMA-2-13B-Chat configurations. New Section 6.4 measures construction, search/optimization, and inference on AG_News with eight examples and one A40; the original A100 inference-only experiment remains. Section 6.1 changes its stated ICV metric from mean accuracy/F1 to accuracy, without establishing reruns. The new permutation experiment's settings are incompletely specified.

E4.justification: New Table 7 tests EQR against partial and full demonstration permutations. Table 5 extends the representation-source ablation to two additional models, and Section 6.4/Table 9 adds analysis of construction and optimization overhead previously excluded from timing comparisons. These substantially broaden the component and efficiency analyses. Original segmentation and transferability questions remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Prompt averaging and varying permutation counts are retained algorithmic analyses, not newly introduced statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds LP averages of 48.56/55.08/61.39 at 4/8/16 shots, additional-model results, permutation scores, and total costs of approximately 19 minutes for DyVec versus 63 for TV and 120 for FV. MTV and per-task FV results disappear from Table 4. Transferability scores are extensively replaced: LLaMA with DX=DY=4 changes from 50.07 to 48.50 on NHSD. Because v2 removes that table's accuracy/F1 metric description, this is not an established performance decline. Original Table 2 rows and generation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same mathematical definitions and relationships. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations; notation and typesetting differences are equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: robust EQR representations, dynamic segmentation and injection, and efficient adaptation outperforming the stated baseline families. The added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 adds an interpretation of total computational savings through REINFORCE optimization versus FV/TV search overhead, extending the previous inference-focused efficiency discussion. The limitations, segmentation interpretation, and transferability explanation otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds LP's frozen-backbone classifier on final hidden representations and removes the MTV description. Section 6.4/Table 9 supplies A40 hardware information and stage-specific runtimes, including approximately 17 minutes for REINFORCE. Existing prompt construction, LoRA settings, and intervention configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds contrastive activation addition and Wang et al. (2025) on defensive steering. The contrastive activation addition work appears under both Panickssery and Rimsky reference entries and should count as one work. The paper's overall positioning against prior ICV methods remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and contribution edits, adds an efficiency subsection and acknowledgments, expands affiliations, and corrects the generation-results cross-reference. The overall narrative, method exposition, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The evaluation displays are substantially revised: Tables 2–3 gain LP rows or a column; Table 4 changes from task-level comparisons to model-level averages; Table 5 expands; and new Tables 7 and 9 display permutation controls and timing breakdowns. Figure 4 is enlarged and repositioned. The existing diagrams and other appendix tables are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The LP comparison, additional models, permutation controls, and full-pipeline timing strengthen empirical support, especially by exposing construction/search costs omitted from v1's inference-only measurements. These gains are limited by removing the close MTV comparator and per-task ICV detail, retaining stale MTV prose, and leaving the revised transferability metric unclear. The permutation table also lacks clear settings: its EQR values match four-shot results despite the section's eight-shot description. Overall, the revision provides useful but qualified improvement.
